name: Citizenship by Descent (Automatic)

qualifying_event.description: Citizenship is conferred automatically at birth (or adoption) in any of several scenarios involving a Bahamian parent.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificate; parents' marriage certificate (where relevant); proof of Bahamian citizenship of the relevant parent.

requirement_groups.name: Born in The Bahamas to married parents, one a citizen

requirements.blocker_text: Born in The Bahamas to married parents with at least one Bahamian citizen parent.

requirement_groups.name: Born to an unmarried Bahamian mother

requirements.blocker_text: Born (in or outside The Bahamas) to an unmarried Bahamian citizen mother.

requirement_groups.name: Born abroad to a married Bahamian father not himself born abroad

requirements.blocker_text: Born outside The Bahamas to a married Bahamian father who was not himself born abroad (i.e. citizenship by descent does not chain a second generation born abroad through the father).
Adopted by a married Bahamian male, or by a single Bahamian female.

evidence_required.document: Proof of the relevant parent's Bahamian citizenship

sources.title: Bahamas Immigration Department -- Pathways to Bahamian Citizenship: automatic citizenship for children born in The Bahamas to married parents with a Bahamian parent, children of unmarried Bahamian mothers, children born abroad to a married Bahamian father not himself born abroad, and adoptees of a married Bahamian male or single Bahamian female

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the Bahamas' initial build. IMPORTANT, well-documented gender asymmetry in Bahamian nationality law: a child born ABROAD to a married Bahamian MOTHER and foreign father does NOT receive automatic citizenship under this framework (that scenario instead routes to PR -- see bs_permanent_residence_general.json's 'children_born_abroad' group -- or to Form IV citizenship registration for minors -- see bs_citizenship_by_registration_family.json), whereas a child born abroad to a married Bahamian FATHER (not himself born abroad) DOES receive automatic citizenship. This asymmetry has been the subject of long-running constitutional-reform debate in the Bahamas (multiple failed referenda) -- flagged here rather than smoothed over, since it materially changes the practical answer depending on which parent is the citizen and whether they are married.
